article.deck: Devon cleared a 51.80 flat-base buy point Oct. 30 and now trades 18.5% below it, under both its 50-day and 200-day lines: not buyable.
body: Devon Energy fell 0.67, or 1.6%, to 42.21 Friday on volume 1.76x its 50-day average. The stock broke out of a seven-week flat base on Oct. 30, clearing the 51.80 buy point on volume 0.91x average, and has given back the whole move in five sessions. It now sits 18.5% below the buy point, well under the 51.80-54.39 buy range. The base was 11.9% deep and formed after a bigger correction: the stock is still under its 52.71 high from March 30, set before a slide to 40.00 on July 2.

The chart has broken down. Devon closed 13.2% below its 50-day line at 48.65 and 8.6% below its 200-day line at 46.17, and it is 2.8 ATRs under the 21-day line at 48.10, with the session's high beneath the line. The stock is 19.9% off its 52-week high. RS rank is 54 of 99 on the desk's list, and the RS line is 30.0% below its high. Devon is down 13.7% in a month, though still up 15.2% this year and 30.5% over 12 months. This is a stalled breakout that has turned into a break of both long lines.

June-quarter EPS rose 44.0% to 2.03 on revenue up 73.1% to $7.417 billion. The three quarters before it posted EPS of 1.09, 0.90 and 0.19, with no year-over-year growth figures given. The desk's calendar had the next report on Nov. 5; none of the headlines in hand covers the results. Devon trades at 7.8 times forward earnings on a $46.4 billion market cap.

MT Newswires' late-afternoon sector update said energy stocks were lower, after an earlier update had them higher Friday afternoon. Devon added 0.37, or 0.9%, to 42.58 after hours as of 6:05 p.m. Eastern.
A close back over the 50-day line would be the first repair; until then there is no buy point in play.

corner.topic: Reading a cup with handle: depth, length, the handle's shakeout, and where the buy point sits
corner.headline: Reading A Cup: Tempus AI Has The Bowl But Not Yet The Handle
corner.deck: Depth, length, the handle's shakeout and the buy point, taught on a 31.0%-deep cup that still has its right side to finish.
body: A cup with handle has four things to read: how deep the cup goes, how long it takes, the handle's shakeout and where the buy point sits. Tempus AI's chart shows three of them today and is still missing the fourth, which makes it a useful chart to open.

Start with depth. Tempus topped at 89.09 on Sept. 29 and fell to 61.51 on Oct. 22, a 31.0% cup. That is deep, though within what O'Neil accepted for a volatile growth stock, and the desk has the market in correction, when bases run deeper. Depth matters because every point lost is overhead the stock has to win back; a cup that cuts too deep leaves the stock needing a recovery before it can break out. The bigger picture makes Tempus deeper still: the cup sits inside a correction from 104.32 on Oct. 9, 2025, to 40.77 on July 28, and the stock is still under that old high.

Next, length. The desk counts the cup at six weeks, 28 sessions. O'Neil wanted a cup to take its time, because a long base lets weak holders sell out and the stock settle. Six weeks is on the short side for a cup with handle, so the right side deserves more patience, not less.

The handle is what Tempus does not have yet. In a finished pattern, the stock climbs the right side of the cup, then drifts lower for a week or more in the upper half of the base before turning up. That drift is the shakeout: it scares out holders who bought near the old high and want to get even, so they are gone before the breakout. A handle should drift, not crash, and should stay in the upper half of the cup; a handle that sinks into the lower half says the base is failing. Friday Tempus closed at 76.05, just into the upper half of a cup that runs from 61.51 to 89.09, and 14.7% below the buy point. It has most of its right side still to build.

Then the buy point. O'Neil puts it ten cents over the handle's high. When a handle's high sits well below the cup's rim, the desk lists the handle high as an early entry and keeps the standard buy point at the rim: Airbnb, today's profile, has a handle high of 179.23 from Oct. 20 and a standard buy point of 193.55. Tempus has no handle, so its buy point is the left-side high, 89.09, plus ten cents: 89.19, with a buy range to 93.65.

Friday's 8.0% jump came on volume 0.91x the 50-day average, after the stock's low touched the 50-day line at 71.32 and it closed above. The desk lists that as an aggressive entry above Friday's high, 76.95, with the line as the stop. That is a separate trade from the cup's buy point, and it carries the risk of buying in the middle of a base that has not finished.

What goes wrong without these rules: a reader who treated Friday's jump as a breakout would own a stock 14.7% below its buy point, with an unfinished right side and no handle, in a market in correction. If Tempus runs straight up the right side and through 89.19 without pausing, that is a cup without a handle, which O'Neil treated as the riskier variant. If it rolls over and loses the 50-day line, the cup gets deeper and the count starts over.
takeaways: Measure depth from the left-side high to the cup's low: Tempus runs 31.0%, from 89.09 to 61.51.
Count the length; a six-week cup like Tempus's is short and needs a well-built right side.
The handle drifts lower in the upper half of the base and shakes out weak holders before the breakout.
The buy point is ten cents over the handle's high, or over the left-side high with no handle: 89.19 for Tempus.
A bounce in the middle of a base is not a breakout; Tempus closed 14.7% below its buy point.
